posts.caption:
70,000 Likes in 1 Sec? 😱

System crash in 1 second!

Most beginners do: UPDATE posts SET likes = likes + 1 ❌
1 post = 1 row lock = All 70k users waiting in queue = DB DEAD.

This is called the Hot Key Problem.

FAANG does this:
1️⃣ Redis - Like goes to cache first, super fast
2️⃣ Sharded Counter - 1 counter → 32 counters, distribute load
3️⃣ Batch Write - Queue (Kafka) → DB writes in bulk
And the secret? For likes, Eventual Consistency is enough! ✅

Interview mein yahi puchte hain!

posts.caption:
If interviewer asks: Access Token vs Refresh Token? 🤔
Explain with example 👇

You login to app → Auth Server gives you 2 tokens:

🔑 Access Token = Temporary Digital Pass (15 mins)
→ Used to access protected APIs (profile, orders)
→ Expires fast = 401 Unauthorized

♻️ Refresh Token = Long-lived (30 days)
→ Job is to get a NEW Access Token
→ Happens in background, no login needed

Security? Access Token = short-lived, limited misuse
Refresh Token = stored securely, can be rotated/revoked

Simple difference:
Access Token → Access APIs
Refresh Token → Get new Access Token

Save this now — you WILL need it before interview.

posts.caption:
90% of devs fail this Flipkart-style interview question. 👇

How do you stop one user from hitting login 1000 times?

Most say “rate limiting” and stop there. The interviewer wants more:

❌ Fixed Window: 100 requests at 11:59:59 + 100 at 12:00:01 = 200 in 2 seconds
✅ Token Bucket: allows normal bursts, enforces the steady limit
⚠️ 10 servers with their own buckets = 1000 requests (fail)
🔥 Fix: one shared bucket in Redis, updated with a Lua script
📩 Always send headers: how many requests are left, and when to retry

Save this before your next interview. 📌

posts.caption:
The BIGGEST AI Problem No One Is Talking About? 👇

It’s called CONTEXT ROT and it’s why your AI gets DUMBER the longer you talk to it.

We think giving AI more info = smarter answers. Wrong.

Research by Chroma (tested 18 frontier models) proved it:
A 300-token focused prompt BEAT a 113k-token long prompt. Every single time.

Why?
Your context window is NOT a storage bin. It’s an attention budget.

Every extra token you add, the AI pays less attention to everything else. It starts forgetting instructions, mixing data, and hallucinating — silently.

This is why your long agents, RAG systems, and 10-page prompts fail.

Fix? Context Engineering > Prompt Engineering.
Save this before your next AI build.

🚀 What really happens behind an OTP screen? 🔐

A premium OTP UI is just the beginning.
Behind that simple screen, the backend handles the complete authentication flow.

Here’s the flow:

1️⃣ User requests an OTP

2️⃣ Backend generates the OTP

3️⃣ OTP is stored securely

4️⃣ Expiration time is set

5️⃣ OTP is sent to the user

6️⃣ User enters the OTP

7️⃣ Backend checks if it exists, is not expired, and matches

8️⃣ ✅ Success → User authenticated

9️⃣ ❌ Failure → Request rejected

🧠 UI → Backend → Verification → Authentication

Good authentication isn’t just about how it looks — it’s about how it works behind the scenes.
